purpose: Forbid any fact about the running system from being established by a constant, a static file, or a registry. A registry declares intent; only observation establishes a fact, and a fact that cannot be observed is unknown with a stated reason, never a silent default. Exists because a measured divergence went undetected for three weeks: a repository registry declared eight nodes with canonical plane keys, the runtime registry loaded six with legacy keys, and the resolver answered a zone that no registry published. Every test passed, because every consumer test reads an inline fixture and every DTO accepts both vocabularies through serde aliases. Nothing compared the sources.
authority: contracts/observability-loop.json stages 1 and 2 — a component is not complete without observation and evaluation.

definitions.declared: A value written by a human or an agent expressing intent. A registry entry, a config key, a constant. It states what should be true.
definitions.observed: A value read from the running substrate during this session, carrying a schema identifier, an observation timestamp, and the identity of the reader.
definitions.fact: A claim about the running system. Every fact must trace to at least one observation. A declaration is not a fact.
definitions.unknown: The state of a fact that was not observed. It is a first-class value carrying the reason it could not be observed. It is never a default, an empty string, a zero, or a null standing in for a successful read.

rules.rule: A registry declares intent; it establishes nothing. Only observation establishes a fact about the running system.
rules.corollary: The forbidden inference is asymmetric and must be stated wherever a registry is read. A node absent from the runtime registry is NOT evidence that it does not exist. A node absent from the desired-state registry IS evidence that it should not exist.
rules.detection: Every registry consumer emits an observation of what it actually resolved, beside what it declared. Drift between the two is an input, not an error.
rules.action: Report the divergence with both values and the reader identity. Never pick a winner silently.
rules.established_by: registry_reconciliation.json finding C1: infra/registry.json declared service.cynic while /etc/cynic/registry.json declared synapse.cynic for the same six nodes at the same addresses, and no surface compared them.

rules.rule: A single observed fact has exactly one owner and one schema, regardless of consumer. A fact may not be established by a constant, a static file, or a registry.
rules.detection: Audit every declared schema identifier. A fact observed by two components with two schemas, or established by a literal, is a violation.
rules.action: Name the owner, then converge the second reader onto the owner's schema. Do not suppress the duplicate.
rules.established_by: 876 declared schema identifiers exist and only 26 of them, 3 percent, are observation or evidence schemas. 799, 91 percent, are exchange contracts and rendered outputs. The system is instrumented to talk, not to see.

rules.rule: A fact that was not observed is unknown with a reason. A default is never substituted for an observation.
rules.detection: Any read path that returns a fallback when the substrate is unreadable is a violation site. This includes unwrap_or on a lookup, a const default where a probe belongs, and a hosts-file entry standing in for a served zone.
rules.action: Return the unknown with its reason. An unknown is a reportable state, not an error to be hidden and not a value to be invented.
rules.established_by: crates/cynic-node/src/network_shadow_proof.rs:118-135 detects and reports three drift kinds, dns_hosts_empty, dns_corefile_empty and dns_resolved_dropin_empty. The system observes its own DNS projection producing nothing and records it as drift rather than resolving it. Separately, crates/cynic-protocol/src/runtime_seed.rs:92 requests a detached signature from https://artifacts.synapse.cynic, which resolves nowhere under any zone. That endpoint was invented as a fixture argument and was never checked.

logging_split.note: the node journals, the substrate and the projection do not. An action decided by the kernel leaves no readable trace on the substrate side.

cynic-cli.note: 729 untyped println calls; the largest single block of unobservable output in the workspace

discovery_surface.note: one discover function exists in cynic-node and it enumerates build targets, not fleet members. No surface reports what is actually running. Fleet membership was established by running pct list on the hypervisor.
discovery_surface.cynic-discovery-host: 220 LOC, and it re-exports adapters from the cynic-host monolith rather than owning discovery, which is also an L1 to L1 DAG inversion

measurement_baseline.silent_evidence: crates/cynic-protocol/src/registry_claim_audit.rs:659 recorded observed: "organ-headscale (not in registry nodes)". The audit saw the divergence and nothing reconciled it.

gaps: no surface reads the hypervisor to compare declared against actual membership, so N5 has no detector
no audit greps /etc/hosts on any node for fleet names the registry does not project
no check fails a build when a registry node name resolves nowhere
729 println calls in cynic-cli emit human text with no schema, so N6 cannot be checked there at all
enforcement.first_enforceable_step: a registry-observation surface that resolves every declared node name, compares it against observed membership from the hypervisor, and emits a schema'd report. cynic-node registry-observation already exists as a surface and is the natural owner.

explicit_non_goals: this contract does not require every value to be dynamic; a compiled constant is legitimate when it is a pure function input with no claim about the running system
it does not require the runtime registry to equal the desired-state registry; they have distinct roles and their lag is the drift to reconcile
it does not prescribe a logging library; it prescribes that an observed fact carries a schema and an owner

verification.logging_split: for c in cynic-cli cynic-node cynic-host cynic-kernel; do printf '%s ' $c; grep -rho '\bprintln!' --include=*.rs crates/$c/src/ | wc -l; done

ratification.status: normative on the operator's instruction of 2026-10-05
ratification.scope_note: N5, N6 and N7 are transverse. The network domain is their first application and its worst current violator, but they govern every crate.
ratification.promotion_note: already written in contracts/ because the operator ruled that a convention which cannot fail a build is prose. The enforcement gaps are stated above rather than implied absent.
